methods.name: track_driver
methods.docs: Build a wired TrackDriver. Wires TrackServiceImpl as Arc<dyn TrackService>, and usecase::fixpoint_resolve_driver::FixpointResolveDriverInteractor (constructed from the four infrastructure::track::fixpoint_resolve_driver adapters -- FsFixpointWorkspaceContextAdapter, FsDryCheckConfigLoaderAdapter, FsFixpointDryGateFactoryAdapter, FsFixpointGateStateFactoryAdapter -- each implementing one fine-grained usecase secondary port) as Arc<dyn FixpointResolveDriverService>, into TrackDriver (IN-12/AC-17). Constructs and injects both -- does not invoke either service itself (ADR 1328 D2: composition root is wire-only). The orchestration itself (repo discovery, base_branch resolution, dry-gate invocation, FixpointResolveService::resolve invocation) lives inside FixpointResolveDriverInteractor (ADR 1328 D4), not in this composition root and not in an infrastructure adapter.

TrackCompositionRoot.docs: Composition root for the track command family. Unit struct: no adapter dependencies injected at construction; all port adapters are wired inline per-method. IN-12/AC-17: the former `fixpoint_resolve` method (which directly constructed and invoked FixpointResolveInteractor, then formatted the result) is removed; the composition root no longer owns any part of the fixpoint-resolve invoke/render path. Orchestration for `sotp track fixpoint-resolve` (repo discovery, base_branch resolution, dry-gate + review + ref-verify gate invocation, FixpointResolveService::resolve invocation) now lives in usecase::fixpoint_resolve_driver::FixpointResolveDriverInteractor (ADR 1328 D4: application orchestration belongs in usecase, not composition or an infrastructure SecondaryAdapter); the four infrastructure::track::fixpoint_resolve_driver adapters it is constructed from each perform only a single narrow I/O concern (ADR 1328 D7: port-impl adapters belong in libs/infrastructure). Render lives in cli_driver::track::TrackDriver. `apps/cli` now dispatches via `TrackCompositionRoot::track_driver().handle(TrackInput::FixpointResolve { .. })` instead of calling this composition root directly. catalogue_lint_check_active_track is merge-inherited from base branch (catalogue-primitive-obsession-guard track); not this track's design work -- grounding stays with this entry's existing spec_refs (IN-05/IN-12/AC-17).

FixpointResolveInput.docs: Superseded by usecase::fixpoint_resolve_driver::FixpointResolveDriverInput (IN-12): `apps/cli` now routes `sotp track fixpoint-resolve` through TrackCompositionRoot::track_driver().handle(TrackInput::FixpointResolve) instead of calling TrackCompositionRoot::fixpoint_resolve(FixpointResolveInput) directly, per no-backward-compat.md (no permanent parallel entrypoint retained). Role note: this entry's role (Dto) is not R1-legal for cli_composition (R1: Dto is forbidden in cli_composition) -- that placement was itself part of the layer violation IN-12 corrects; recorded here for audit-trail accuracy of the removed item, not as an endorsed placement. The former method's wiring, invoke, and render responsibilities are now split across three layers per ADR 1328 D2/D3/D4: the four fine-grained infrastructure::track::fixpoint_resolve_driver adapters (FsFixpointWorkspaceContextAdapter / FsDryCheckConfigLoaderAdapter / FsFixpointDryGateFactoryAdapter / FsFixpointGateStateFactoryAdapter, each implementing one usecase secondary port; R1: SecondaryAdapter is infrastructure-only) perform only narrow I/O concerns and do not invoke FixpointResolveService; the actual orchestration and FixpointResolveService::resolve invocation live in usecase::fixpoint_resolve_driver::FixpointResolveDriverInteractor (ADR 1328 D4: application orchestration belongs in usecase, not composition or an infrastructure SecondaryAdapter -- an earlier draft that pushed this invocation into a single infrastructure adapter was flagged as a D4 violation, 2026-07-02 plan-artifacts final-review P1 finding, and corrected here); TrackCompositionRoot::track_driver() only constructs and injects the four adapters plus the interactor built from them (wire-only, ADR 1328 D2) and never invokes FixpointResolveDriverService itself. This differs from the pre-existing TrackServiceImpl (genuinely pub, out of this track's IN/AC scope, and structurally coupled to TrackCompositionRoot because each method calls TrackCompositionRoot::new().track_*()), so it is not relocatable to infrastructure without further restructuring and is left as an out-of-scope pre-existing gap, not a pattern to replicate here. DryDriverAdapter (like DryFixRunnerCompositionRoot, renamed CodexDryFixLocalRunner) has since relocated to libs/infrastructure (infrastructure::dry_check::dry_fix_local::{DryDriverAdapter, CodexDryFixLocalRunner}, ADR 1328 D7), so neither is a cli_composition type any more; DryDriverAdapter is no longer crate-private -- it is a public infrastructure SecondaryAdapter declared in infrastructure-types.json. The four fixpoint-resolve adapters have no such composition-root dependency (their wiring logic uses only domain / usecase / infrastructure types), so they follow the D7 default placement.

methods.name: dry_driver
methods.docs: Construct a wired `cli_driver::dry::DryDriver` for injection into the CLI. IN-14/AC-20: dry_write / dry_results / dry_check_approved are removed from this type (see below) -- this method is the ONLY remaining public surface for the whole `dry` family, and its own wiring grows to also construct the infrastructure::dry_check::dry_driver_shared / dry_write_driver adapters (infrastructure::dry_check::dry_driver_shared::FsDryRepoRootAdapter / FsDryBaseBranchAdapter / FsDryCheckStorageFactoryAdapter / FsDryDiffBaseFactoryAdapter shared across all three new interactors; infrastructure::dry_check::dry_write_driver::FsDryWriteConfigLoaderAdapter / FsDryCorpusFragmentsAdapter / DryCheckServiceFactoryAdapter / FsDryCorpusRootManifestAdapter for write_service only -- infrastructure::dry_check::dry_write_driver::RecordingDryTierTelemetryAdapter is NOT constructed here -- it is constructed internally by DryCheckServiceFactoryAdapter::build, not by this composition root) plus the three new usecase::dry_write_driver::DryWriteDriverInteractor / usecase::dry_results_driver::DryResultsDriverInteractor / usecase::dry_check_approved_driver::DryCheckApprovedDriverInteractor instances (injecting infrastructure::dry_check::dry_driver_shared::FsDryDiffBaseFactoryAdapter for DryCheckApprovedDriverInteractor's diff-base factory dependency, which constructs infrastructure::dry_check::diff_base_resolver::FsDiffBaseResolverAdapter per request after the base branch is resolved; reusing the existing infrastructure::dry_check::FsDryCorpusMetaAdapter and the existing usecase::dry_check::fragment_pipeline::DryFragmentPipelineInteractor + infrastructure::dry_check::GitDryCheckDiffGetter / infrastructure::semantic_dup::CodeFragmentExtractorAdapter for DryCheckApprovedDriverInteractor's fragment_pipeline dependency; and injecting the existing infrastructure::track::fixpoint_resolve_driver::FsDryCheckConfigLoaderAdapter-equivalent usecase::fixpoint_resolve_driver::DryCheckConfigLoaderPort adapter for DryCheckApprovedDriverInteractor's config_loader dependency -- constructed inline here the same way, not re-exported). usecase::dry_check_approved_driver::DryCheckApprovedDriverInteractor::new takes only the seven fine-grained secondary ports above (no clock or telemetry port -- usecase-purity forbids sampling std::time::Instant or invoking a telemetry port from inside a usecase entrypoint); the resulting interactor is passed unwrapped as `check_approved_service` with no telemetry adapter constructed or injected alongside it: `cli_driver::dry::DryDriver::new` takes only the four services (`service`, `write_service`, `results_service`, `check_approved_service`), dropping the `check_approved_telemetry` parameter and the infrastructure::dry_check::dry_check_approved_driver::DryGateEvalTelemetryAdapter it used to wire (both existed briefly in an earlier IN-14 draft and were retracted). Wall-clock timing measurement and `GateEval` telemetry emission for `dry check-approved` now live entirely in the bin layer (`apps/cli/src/commands/dry.rs::execute_dry_check_approved`), calling `cli_composition::telemetry_wiring::{resolve_telemetry_writer, emit_gate_eval}` directly with no Port abstraction at this boundary, mirroring `execute_verify_with_telemetry` -- superseding a still-earlier design where an infrastructure-hosted TimedGateEvalDryCheckApprovedService decorator implemented the primary DryCheckApprovedDriverService port to bolt timing onto it, which was a layer-boundary violation. This method continues to only wire and inject (ADR 1328 D2); it never invokes any of the four services itself.

methods.name: git_switch_and_pull_in
methods.docs: Anchor `git switch` + `git pull` to a specific project checkout instead of the CWD. Callers that resolve the requested checkout via `--project-root` (e.g. `sotp track switch-base --project-root /path/to/checkout`) must reach git via this entry point so the underlying git commands run against the requested worktree, not the process CWD.

methods.name: git_unstage
methods.docs: Unstage paths (remove from git index without discarding worktree changes).

methods.name: current_branch_track_id_strict
methods.docs: Resolve the track ID from the current git branch (strict mode). Returns `Ok(Some(id))` only when the branch matches `track/<id>` and the id is valid. Non-track branches (e.g. `main`) return `Ok(None)`. Returns `Err` when the branch matches `track/<id>` but the `<id>` fails validation.

GitCompositionRoot.docs: Composition root for the `git` command family. Unit struct: no adapter dependencies are injected at construction time. IN-05: `git_switch_and_pull_in` (added in this track) anchors `git switch` + `git pull` to an explicit `project_root` instead of the process CWD, so `TrackCompositionRoot::track_switch_base` can operate correctly when invoked with `--project-root`. The pre-existing `git_switch_and_pull` now delegates to a private `git_switch_and_pull_impl` helper shared with the new method; the helper is not part of the public API surface and is not catalogued.

DryFixRunnerCompositionRoot.docs: Composition root for the `dry_fix_runner` command family (`sotp dry fix-local`), as it existed earlier in this track (previously declared here as `action: reference`, since `dry_fix_runner.rs` was byte-identical to `main` at that point). Superseded by relocation: `apps/cli-composition/src/dry_fix_runner.rs` and its sibling `apps/cli-composition/src/dry_driver_adapter.rs` are both deleted; the struct is renamed to `CodexDryFixLocalRunner` and, together with `DryDriverAdapter`, relocated to `libs/infrastructure/src/dry_check/dry_fix_local/` (ADR 1328 D7: port-impl adapters belong in libs/infrastructure). Role note: this entry's `CompositionRoot` role was fully R1-legal while the type lived in cli_composition (`CompositionRoot` is cli_composition ONLY); the relocated `CodexDryFixLocalRunner` carries `role: SecondaryAdapter` instead, per infrastructure's R1 role set (recorded here for audit-trail accuracy of the removed item, not as an endorsed placement for a hypothetical CompositionRoot-in-infrastructure). See infrastructure-types.json's `CodexDryFixLocalRunner` / `DryDriverAdapter` entries for the new declarations.
